newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NEXT MOVE IN RATES UP, BUT NOT JUST YET-PBB BANKER.
newsitem.headline: NEXT MOVE IN RATES UP, BUT NOT JUST YET-PBB BANKER.

text.p: The next move in interest rates will be up, but with unemployment stubbornly high and inflation historically low, there is no imminent need for rate increases, the chief executive officer of Paribas Bank Belgium said.

"With rates at around three percent, the probability of higher rates is higher than that of lower rates...that is logical. But there is no reason why rates should go higher now," Philippe Romagnoli told a news conference on PBB's 1996 results.
The Belgian central bank's key central rate, which applies to overnight lending for primary government debt dealers and is closely tied to Bundesbank rates, is currently at three percent.
